\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تحقيق} (taḥqīq)}{تحقيق (taḥqīq)}]{\ar{تحقيق} (taḥqīq) — an investigation, an inquiry}

\label{lesson:AR-C308-tahqiq}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a battle, then the Arabic for to wage war.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تحقيق}}
\textbf{\ar{تحقيق}} — \emph{taḥqīq} — \textquotedblleft{}an investigation, an inquiry\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{بدأت} \ar{الشرطة} \ar{تحقيقا} \ar{في} \ar{الحادث}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{badaʾat ash-shurṭa taḥqīqan fī al-ḥādith.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The police opened an investigation into the accident.
\end{quote}

Plural \ar{تحقيقات}. In the press, a \ar{تحقيق} is an investigative report.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تحقيق}} (\emph{taḥqīq}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ḥ-q-q} (Lane), the root of \emph{ḥaqq}, truth and right. \emph{Taḥqīq} is the verbal noun of Form II: \textquotedblleft{}making sure of the truth\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taḥqīq}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taḥqīq}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{badaʾat ash-shurṭa taḥqīqan fī al-ḥādith.} — The police opened an investigation into the accident.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a battle, then the Arabic for to wage war, then say \emph{taḥqīq} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{تحقيق} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An investigation, an inquiry\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{حقق} (ḥaqqaqa)}{حقق (ḥaqqaqa)}]{\ar{حقق} (ḥaqqaqa) — to investigate; to achieve}

\label{lesson:AR-C308-haqqaqa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to wage war, then the Arabic for an investigation.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{حقق}}
\textbf{\ar{حقق}} — \emph{ḥaqqaqa} — \textquotedblleft{}to investigate; to achieve\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{حققت} \ar{الشرطة} \ar{مع} \ar{الحارس}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ḥaqqaqat ash-shurṭa maʿa al-ḥāris.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The police questioned the guard.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يحقق}, \emph{yuḥaqqiq}.

\ar{حقق} \ar{مع} someone: to question them. \ar{حقق} \ar{هدفه}: he reached his goal.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{حقق}} (\emph{ḥaqqaqa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ḥ-q-q} (Lane), the root of \emph{ḥaqq}, truth. It is Form II, \textquotedblleft{}to make sure of; to make come true\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḥaqqaqa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḥaqqaqa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḥaqqaqat ash-shurṭa maʿa al-ḥāris.} — The police questioned the guard.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to wage war, then the Arabic for an investigation, then say \emph{ḥaqqaqa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{حقق} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To investigate; to achieve\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{محقق} (muḥaqqiq)}{محقق (muḥaqqiq)}]{\ar{محقق} (muḥaqqiq) — an investigator, a detective}

\label{lesson:AR-C308-muhaqqiq}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for an investigation, then the Arabic for to investigate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{محقق}}
\textbf{\ar{محقق}} — \emph{muḥaqqiq} — \textquotedblleft{}an investigator, a detective\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{سأل} \ar{المحقق} \ar{الجيران} \ar{عن} \ar{الحريق}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{saʾala al-muḥaqqiq al-jīrān ʿan al-ḥarīq.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The investigator asked the neighbours about the fire.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{محقق}} (\emph{muḥaqqiq}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ḥ-q-q} (Lane), the root of \emph{ḥaqq}, truth. \emph{Muḥaqqiq} is the Form II participle, \textquotedblleft{}one who makes sure of the truth\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{muḥaqqiq}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{muḥaqqiq}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{saʾala al-muḥaqqiq al-jīrān ʿan al-ḥarīq.} — The investigator asked the neighbours about the fire.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for an investigation, then the Arabic for to investigate, then say \emph{muḥaqqiq} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{محقق} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An investigator, a detective\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{دليل} (dalīl)}{دليل (dalīl)}]{\ar{دليل} (dalīl) — evidence, proof; a guide}

\label{lesson:AR-C308-dalil}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to investigate, then the Arabic for an investigator.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{دليل}}
\textbf{\ar{دليل}} — \emph{dalīl} — \textquotedblleft{}evidence, proof; a guide\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{وجد} \ar{المحقق} \ar{دليلا} \ar{في} \ar{الغرفة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{wajada al-muḥaqqiq dalīlan fī al-ghurfa.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The investigator found a piece of evidence in the room.
\end{quote}

Plural: \ar{أدلة}, \emph{adilla}.

Also a guidebook or a guide: \ar{دليل} \ar{سياحي}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{دليل}} (\emph{dalīl}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{d-l-l} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to direct, to show the way\textquotedblright{}. A \emph{dalīl} is what points the way to a place, or to the truth.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dalīl}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dalīl}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{wajada al-muḥaqqiq dalīlan fī al-ghurfa.} — The investigator found a piece of evidence in the room.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to investigate, then the Arabic for an investigator, then say \emph{dalīl} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{دليل} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Evidence, proof; a guide\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{بصمة} (baṣma)}{بصمة (baṣma)}]{\ar{بصمة} (baṣma) — a fingerprint}

\label{lesson:AR-C308-basma}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for an investigator, then the Arabic for evidence.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{بصمة}}
\textbf{\ar{بصمة}} — \emph{baṣma} — \textquotedblleft{}a fingerprint\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{وجدت} \ar{الشرطة} \ar{بصمة} \ar{على} \ar{الباب}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{wajadat ash-shurṭa baṣma ʿalā al-bāb.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The police found a fingerprint on the door.
\end{quote}

Plural \ar{بصمات}. \ar{بصمة} \ar{الإصبع} in full.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{بصمة}} (\emph{baṣma}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{b-ṣ-m} (Lane), where \emph{buṣm} is the span between the little finger and the third finger spread apart. \emph{Baṣma}, a fingerprint, is a modern sense.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{baṣma}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{baṣma}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{wajadat ash-shurṭa baṣma ʿalā al-bāb.} — The police found a fingerprint on the door.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for an investigator, then the Arabic for evidence, then say \emph{baṣma} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{بصمة} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A fingerprint\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(dialogue)]{Words from chapters 301–308 — a review}

\label{lesson:AR-R308-review-301-308}



\begin{quote}
Say the Arabic for to collide and to overturn.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item to collide, to overturn, a victim, a wounded person, to give first aid
  \item a dialogue, to hold a dialogue, to conduct, to host, a spokesperson
  \item a legend, a myth, a hero, a villain, to imagine
  \item an age, long ago, an era, at that time, a reign
  \item a court of law, an eyewitness, to accuse, a defendant, to pass judgment
  \item a wedding feast, to propose marriage, an engagement to marry, to escort a bride, to ululate for joy
  \item an army, a soldier, a war, a battle, to wage war
  \item an investigation, to investigate, an investigator, evidence, a fingerprint
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
To collide? (\textbf{\ar{اصطدم}}, \emph{iṣṭadama}.) To overturn? (\textbf{\ar{انقلب}}, \emph{inqalaba}.) A victim? (\textbf{\ar{ضحية}}, \emph{ḍaḥiyya}.) A wounded person? (\textbf{\ar{جريح}}, \emph{jarīḥ}.) To give first aid? (\textbf{\ar{أسعف}}, \emph{asʿafa}.) A dialogue? (\textbf{\ar{حوار}}, \emph{ḥiwār}.) To hold a dialogue? (\textbf{\ar{حاور}}, \emph{ḥāwara}.) To conduct? (\textbf{\ar{أجرى}}, \emph{ajrā}.) To host? (\textbf{\ar{استضاف}}, \emph{istaḍāfa}.) A spokesperson? (\textbf{\ar{متحدث}}, \emph{mutaḥaddith}.) A legend? (\textbf{\ar{أسطورة}}, \emph{usṭūra}.) A myth? (\textbf{\ar{خرافة}}, \emph{khurāfa}.) A hero? (\textbf{\ar{بطل}}, \emph{baṭal}.) A villain? (\textbf{\ar{شرير}}, \emph{shirrīr}.) To imagine? (\textbf{\ar{تخيل}}, \emph{takhayyala}.) An age? (\textbf{\ar{زمن}}, \emph{zaman}.) Long ago? (\textbf{\ar{منذ} \ar{زمن} \ar{طويل}}, \emph{mundhu zaman ṭawīl}.) An era? (\textbf{\ar{حقبة}}, \emph{ḥiqba}.) At that time? (\textbf{\ar{آنذاك}}, \emph{ānadhāk}.) A reign? (\textbf{\ar{عهد}}, \emph{ʿahd}.) A court of law? (\textbf{\ar{محكمة}}, \emph{maḥkama}.) An eyewitness? (\textbf{\ar{شاهد} \ar{عيان}}, \emph{shāhid ʿiyān}.) To accuse? (\textbf{\ar{اتهم}}, \emph{ittahama}.) A defendant? (\textbf{\ar{متهم}}, \emph{muttaham}.) To pass judgment? (\textbf{\ar{حكم}}, \emph{ḥakama}.) A wedding feast? (\textbf{\ar{عرس}}, \emph{ʿurs}.) To propose marriage? (\textbf{\ar{خطب}}, \emph{khaṭaba}.) An engagement to marry? (\textbf{\ar{خطوبة}}, \emph{khuṭūba}.) To escort a bride? (\textbf{\ar{زف}}, \emph{zaffa}.) To ululate for joy? (\textbf{\ar{زغرد}}, \emph{zaghrada}.) An army? (\textbf{\ar{جيش}}, \emph{jaysh}.) A soldier? (\textbf{\ar{جندي}}, \emph{jundī}.) A war? (\textbf{\ar{حرب}}, \emph{ḥarb}.) A battle? (\textbf{\ar{معركة}}, \emph{maʿraka}.) To wage war? (\textbf{\ar{حارب}}, \emph{ḥāraba}.) An investigation? (\textbf{\ar{تحقيق}}, \emph{taḥqīq}.) To investigate? (\textbf{\ar{حقق}}, \emph{ḥaqqaqa}.) An investigator? (\textbf{\ar{محقق}}, \emph{muḥaqqiq}.) Evidence? (\textbf{\ar{دليل}}, \emph{dalīl}.) A fingerprint? (\textbf{\ar{بصمة}}, \emph{baṣma}.)
